analysis.text: A) 张冠李戴 Having one's basic needs covered while away from home. 盗用了原文 the basic needs like toilet and showers are covered；但说在意 basic needs 的是男方（M），不 是女方，题目问的是女方觉得什么吸引人，人物错位。 借用原文：the basic needs like toilet and showers are covered C) 偷换概念 Slowing down in one's increasingly hectic life. 借用了原文 Slow down 里的 slow down；但那是女方让激动的男方“别急、慢点说”，是对话节奏用语，根本不是她觉得吸引 人的生活理念，把口语提醒偷换成人生主张。 借用原文：Slow down D) 张冠李戴 Riding one's mountain bike on vacation. 盗用了原文 my mountain bike；但提山地车 的是男方（担心装不装得下），与女方“觉得吸引人”毫无关系，人物和语境都错。 借用原文：my mountain bike 1 W: You wanted to see me? But if you needed some leave, why didn't you ask for it earlier? M: 当然可以。但如果你需要休假，为什么不早点提出来呢？ Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 7 W: I'm not sure why. I guess I kind of felt bad asking for it. W: 我也不知道为什么。我想我大概觉得提这个要求有点不好意思。 8 M: You shouldn't feel bad asking for leave, especially if you need it. M: 你不该为请假感到不好意思，尤其是你确实需要的时候。 9 W: I know. W: 足够了。我确定。 14 M: Okay, good. So this is what we're going to do. You will take those days off, and I expect that you will gradually come back to your usual self. questions.answerText: The woman will be off work on the next two Mondays.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: W: Would it be possible to take the next two Mondays off? ... M: Sure thing. ... M: So this is what we're going to do. You will take those days off, and I expect that you will gradually come back to your usual self. 女：能让我接下来两个周一请假吗？……男：当然可以。……男：那我们就这么办，你把那两 天休掉，我希望你慢慢恢复到平时的状态。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 请求—应允—拍板三处合一。女方提出 take the next two Mondays off，男方 Sure thing 应允，结尾再 So this is what we're going to do. You will take those days off 拍板；"请 求被应允并在结尾确认"是约定题的答案信号。

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 A 说 resume her work in two weeks（两周后复工），但原文女方只是休"两个周一"、并 非停工两周后才回来；"two"原词在，时间概念却被偷换，且 in two months 才是再约谈时 间，A 张冠时间。 借用原文：take the next two Mondays off B) 张冠李戴 B 说 The man will be back at his 100%，但原文 What I need is for you to be back at your 100% 是男方要求"你（女方）"回到100%，主语该是女方不是男方；盗用 100% 原词 却把人安反，属张冠李戴。 借用原文：What I need is for you to be back at your 100% D) 过度推断 D 说 The man will help the woman get back to her usual self，但原文是男方期望"你会 慢慢恢复"you will gradually come back to your usual self，是女方自己恢复，并非男 方"帮"她；盗 usual self 原词却脑补出"帮助"，属过度推断。 借用原文：you will gradually come back to your usual self Section B 1 There are many factors that impact our health. These include our finances, our emotions and the way we work. Education is one such factor. Research suggests that higher levels of education can lead to better health and even greater longevity. But what about the education of your partner? New research seeks to answer this question. Researchers use data from a longitudinal study. The data came from surveys first administered to high school seniors in 1957. The surveys ended in 2011. The team found that a person whose spouse had a higher level of education tended to report better health. This remained the case when adjusting for other factors, such as participants' own education, social background and health status before and after marriage. The authors suggest that high levels of education provide shared social, intellectual, emotional and financial resources. These include things like higher levels of emotional intelligence, particular skills or knowledge, or more money. The researchers concede that an individual's own level of education is clearly important for their health, but they assert that individuals also can reap the benefits of their partner's education. It is noteworthy that the effects vary by gender. One popular theory is that it's a case of too low wages for jobs that don't require a degree. An alternate theory is that there were more jobs not requiring a college degree in the past than now. 究竟是什么导致了这种下降？嗯，几十年来经济学家一直在努力确定这种下降的根源，并提出了几种理 论。一种流行的理论是，不需要学位的工作工资过低。另一种理论是，过去不需要大学学位的工作比现在 更多。 3 A recent working paper from the National Bureau of Economic Research reviewed those theories and put forward additional hypotheses about the causes of the problem. Let's look at that paper now. First, the researchers considered the issue of wages. As the wage gap has grown between those with college degrees and those without, economists have suggested that men aren't as interested in taking some of the less lucrative jobs. While the authors of the paper found truth in this explanation, they assert that low wages can't be the only factor, as wages for men without college degrees, adjusting for inflation, haven't changed much since the 1960s, making it hard to see why fewer men seem willing to accept those wages. 美国国家经济研究局最近的一篇工作论文审视了这些理论，并提出了关于问题成因的其他假设。现在让我 们看看那篇论文。首先,研究人员考虑了工资问题。随着拥有大学学位者与没有大学学位者之间的工资差距 扩大,经济学家认为男性对接受一些收入较低的工作不那么感兴趣。虽然论文作者认为这一解释有其道理, 但他们断言低工资不可能是唯一因素,因为没有大学学位的男性的工资,经通货膨胀调整后,自20世纪60年代 以来并没有太大变化,这使得很难理解为什么似乎越来越少的男性愿意接受这些工资。 4 This leads to the second theory, that more jobs require a college degree today than in the past. Indeed, that theory seems valid, because in America today, 2/3 of jobs are filled by workers with at least some college education. However, the authors of the paper argue that there are other factors amplifying the problem. 这引出了第二种理论,即如今需要大学学位的工作比过去更多。确实,这一理论似乎是有效的,因为在今天的 美国,三分之二的工作由至少接受过一些大学教育的工人担任。然而,论文作者认为还有其他因素在放大这 个问题。 5 They identified two new potential explanations: the first being the tremendous decline in marriage among men without college degrees since the 1960s; and the second being the increase in women participating in the workforce that was concurrent with the decline in marriage. These two changes mean that men might not have families to support, or if they do, their wives might be doing more of the providing, both of which might remove the financial incentive to work. The authors of the paper concede that research on the subject isn't complete, but they argue that their work supports the value of a college education. 他们确定了两个新的潜在解释:第一个是自20世纪60年代以来没有大学学位的男性结婚率大幅下降;第二个 是与结婚率下降同时发生的女性劳动力参与率的增加。这两个变化意味着男性可能没有家庭需要供养,或者 即使有,他们的妻子可能承担更多的供养责任,这两种情况都可能消除工作的经济激励。论文作者承认关于 这一主题的研究尚未完成,但他们认为他们的工作支持大学教育的价值。

Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard. 3 In a 2015 survey for YouGov, 65% of British people and 81% of the French said they thought the world was getting worse. Why? 在2015年YouGov的一项调查中,65%的英国人和81%的法国人表示他们认为世界正在变得更糟。然而,根 据众多可靠的统计数据,这些人完全错了。没有一个头脑正常的人会希望生活在前几个世纪。然而人们确实 这样希望。为什么? 4 Our prevailing mood of despair is irrational. It says more about us than it does about how things really are. It is best explained as the result of various psychological biases that served a purpose for our evolutionary ancestors—but now, in a media-saturated era, constantly mislead us. Once upon a time, it was of great survival value to be worried about everything that could go wrong. This is what makes bad news especially compelling. 我们普遍的绝望情绪是不理性的。它更多地反映了我们自身,而非事物的真实状况。最好的解释是,这是各 种心理偏见的结果,这些偏见曾对我们进化中的祖先有用,但现在在一个媒体饱和的时代,却不断误导我们。 曾几何时,担心可能出错的一切事情具有极大的生存价值。这就是坏消息特别引人注目的原因。 5 In our evolutionary past, it was a very good thing that our attention could be easily seized by negative information, since it might well indicate a dangerous risk to our own survival. The caveman who always assumed there was a lion behind the next rock would usually be wrong, but he'd be much more likely to survive and reproduce than one who always assumed the opposite. But that was all before newspapers, television and the internet. In today's hyper connected times, our addiction to bad news just leads us to vacuum up depressing or enraging stories from across the globe. Whether these news stories threaten us or not, we conclude that things are much worse than they actually are. Really good news, on the other hand, can be a lot harder to spot in a newspaper because predictable daily events by definition aren't news. 在我们的进化历史中,我们的注意力很容易被负面信息吸引是一件非常好的事情,因为它很可能预示着对我 们自身生存的危险风险。那个总是假设下一块岩石后面有狮子的穴居人通常会判断错误,但他比总是做相反 假设的人更有可能生存和繁衍。但那都是在报纸、电视和互联网出现之前。在当今这个高度互联的时代,我 们对坏消息的沉迷只会导致我们从全球各地吸收令人沮丧或愤怒的故事。无论这些新闻是否威胁到我们,我 们都会得出结论:事情比实际情况糟糕得多。另一方面,真正的好消息在报纸上可能更难发现,因为可预测的 日常事件从定义上讲不是新闻。

What do we learn about the "natural world" characterized by Thomas Hobbes? A) It gets misrepresented by philosophers and anthropologists. B) It gets distorted in Darwin's The Origin of Species. C) It is free from the rational intervention of humans. D) It is the pre-rational world rarely appreciated nowadays.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Thomas Hobbes, one of the great philosophers of the seventeenth century, is perhaps best remembered for his characterization of the "natural world," that is, the world before the imposition of the will of humanity, as being "nasty, brutish, and short." Thomas Hobbes 这位 17 世纪的大哲学家，最为人记得的或许是他对"自然世界"——也就 是人类意志介入之前的世界——的刻画："令人厌恶、野蛮且短暂"。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 无中生有 It gets misrepresented by philosophers and anthropologists.说自然世界被哲学家 和人类学家"歪曲表述"——但原文只说 Hobbes 这一形象"被达尔文的工作强 化"（reinforced by Charles Darwin's highly influential work），后来又说当代人类 学研究"质疑了这一观点"（questioned），并没有说 Hobbes 关于 natural world 的描 述被哲学家和人类学家共同歪曲。属无中生有。 B) 与原文相反 It gets distorted in Darwin's The Origin of Species.说自然世界在达尔文的书里被歪 曲——但原文是This image of the pre-rational world is still widely held, reinforced by Charles Darwin's highly influential work，达尔文是"加强"而非"歪曲"，方向相 反。属与原文相反。 C) ✓ 正确 the world before the imposition of the will of humanity ↔ It is free from the rational intervention of humans. 预判要求答案体现"无人类理性介入"这一特征；It is free from the rational intervention of humans.正是同位语的直接同义改写——free from 完美匹配 before （按时间顺序的不及）。 D) 与原文相反 It is the pre-rational world rarely appreciated nowadays.说 pre-rational world"当 今很少受到欣赏"——但原文紧接着说This image of the pre-rational world is still widely held，明确说这一形象"仍被广泛持有"，与选项的 rarely 完全对立。属与原文 相反。 从Darwin在《物种起源》中的论断我们可以得出什么结论? A) 所有物种本质上都依赖其他物种生存。 B) 生存斗争并不排斥相互支持。 C) 作为生存策略,竞争与合作同等重要。 D) 最强的物种被证明是自然选择中最适合的。

questions.stem: What can we conclude from Darwin's assertion in The Origin of Species?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: 题干What can we conclude from Darwin's assertion in The Origin of Species?用 conclude from 引导，要求从达尔文的断言中得出结论，属于"一步推断题"。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: Q54主干是 What can we conclude from Darwin's assertion；in The Origin of Species 是地点状语限定该断言出自哪本书。conclude from 重在"从断言本身推出"，所以答案必须 紧贴 Darwin 那句原话，不能拿别的句子做依据。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Darwin asserted in The Origin of Species that the struggles he was describing should be viewed as metaphors and could easily include dependence and cooperation. 达尔文在《物种起源》中断言：他所描述的那些斗争应当被视为隐喻，完全可以涵盖依赖与 合作。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 过度推断 All species inherently depend on others for survival.中 All species（所有物种）+ inherently（天生地）是绝对化用语；原文只是说"斗争可以包含依赖与合作"，并未推 出"所有物种都天生依赖他者才能生存"。属过度推断。 B) ✓ 正确 the struggles he was describing should be viewed as metaphors and could easily include dependence and cooperation ↔Struggles for survival do not exclude mutual support. 预判说斗争不排斥互助；Struggles for survival do not exclude mutual support.中 do not exclude 与原文 could include 等值，mutual support 概括 dependence and cooperation，逻辑等值、范围一致。 C) 过度推断 Competition weighs as much as cooperation as a survival strategy.中"竞争与合作 作为生存策略权重相当"，把两者并列等值——但原文只说斗争"可以包含"合作，并未 在"权重相当"的层面比较两者；权重比较是凭空引入。属过度推断。 D) 偷换概念 The strongest species proves to be the fittest in natural selection.说"最强的物种被 证明是最适合的"——但原文的关键点是"survival of the fittest 这个短语达尔文自己从 未使用"，且本句要的是"Darwin's assertion"（达尔文的断言），不是社会上对"适者生 存"的概括；况且 fittest 也不等于 strongest，原文专门指出自然选择并不暗示竞争才是 最优策略。属偷换概念。 Margaret Mead在研究了数十种不同文化后得出了什么结论? A) 具有竞争性是人类的特征。 B) 美国人独特地反对合作。 C) 竞争在西方社会中相对更为普遍。 55. What conclusion did Margaret Mead reach after studying dozens of different cultures? A) It is characteristic of humans to be competitive. B) Americans are uniquely opposed to cooperation. C) Competition is relatively more prevalent in Western societies. D) People's attitude towards competition is actually culture-bound. D) 人们对竞争的态度实际上受文化束缚。

questions.stem: What conclusion did Margaret Mead reach after studying dozens of different cultures?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: 题干What conclusion did Margaret Mead reach after studying dozens of different cultures?问"Mead 得出了什么结论"，是对原文最后一句明文表达的结论的复述，属于细 节题。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: Q55主干是 What conclusion did Margaret Mead reach；after studying dozens of different cultures 是时间状语。注意问的是"Mead 的结论"，所以答案必须是 Mead's final conclusion 那一句的同义改写，而不是 Mead 研究过程的具体发现（那是中间结论， 不是 final conclusion）。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: After studying dozens of such cultures, Mead's final conclusion was that competitiveness is a culturally created aspect of human behavior, and that its prevalence in a particular society is relative to how that society values it. 在研究了数十个这样的文化之后，Mead 的最终结论是：竞争性是人类行为中由文化塑造出 的一面；它在某个具体社会中的普遍程度，取决于该社会对它的评价。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 与原文相反 It is characteristic of humans to be competitive.说"竞争是人类的天性"——但这正是 Mead 想要驳斥的观点，Mead 的结论恰恰相反：竞争性不是天生的，而是文化塑造 的。属与原文相反。 B) 偷换概念 Americans are uniquely opposed to cooperation.说美国人"独一无二地反对合 作"——但原文是Americans uniquely praise competition as natural, inevitable, and desirable，说美国人独一无二地"赞美竞争"，并未说他们反对合作；"赞美 X"与"反对 Y"不可直接对调。属偷换概念。 C) 过度推断 Competition is relatively more prevalent in Western societies.说"竞争在西方社会中 相对更普遍"——但 Mead 的最终结论是"竞争普遍程度取决于社会评价"，并未把社会 分成"西方/非西方"两类、也未声称"竞争在西方更普遍"是普遍规律。属过度推断兼以偏 概全。 D) ✓ 正确 competitiveness is a culturally created aspect of human behavior ↔ People's attitude towards competition is actually culture-bound. its prevalence in a particular society is relative to how that society values it ↔ actually culture-bound 预判要求答案体现"竞争性受文化决定"；People's attitude towards competition is actually culture-bound.中 culture-bound 直接等值于 culturally created，是 Mead 结论的最简同义改写。

A) Most visitors come to Cape Canaveral, on the northeast coast of Florida, for the tourist attractions. It's home to the second-busiest cruise ship port in the world and is a gateway to the cosmos. Nearly 1.5 million visitors flock here every year to watch rockets, spacecraft, and satellites blast off into the solar system from Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex. Nearly 64 kilometers of undeveloped beach and 648 square kilometers of protected refuge fan out from the cape's sandy shores.
B) Yet some of Cape Canaveral's most legendary attractions lie unseen, wedged under the sea's surface in mud and sand, for this part of the world has a reputation as a deadly ship trap. Over the centuries, dozens of majestic Old World sailing ships smashed and sank on this irregular stretch of windy Florida coast. They were vessels built for war and commerce, crossing the globe carrying everything from coins to cannons, boxes of silver and gold, chests of jewels and porcelain, and pearls from the Caribbean.
C) Cape Canaveral contains one of the greatest concentrations of colonial shipwrecks in the world. In recent years, advances in radar, diving, detection equipment, computers, and GPS have transformed the hunt. The naked eye might see a pile of rocks, but technology can reveal the precious artifacts(人 工制品) that lie hidden on the ocean floor.
D) As technology renders the seabed more accessible, the hunt for treasure-filled ships has drawn a fresh tide of salvors(打捞人员) and their investors—as well as marine archaeologists(考古学家) wanting to bring to light the lost relics. But of late, when salvors have found vessels, their rights have been challenged in court. The big question: who should have control of these treasures?
E) High-stakes fights over shipwrecks pit archaeologists against treasure hunters in a vicious cycle of accusations. Archaeologists regard themselves as protectors of history, and they see salvors as careless destroyers. Salvors feel they do the hard work of searching for ships, only to have them stolen from under them when discovered. This kind of clash inevitably takes place on a grand scale. Aside from the salvors, their investors, and the maritime archaeologists who serve as expert witnesses, the battles sweep in local and international governments and organizations like UNESCO that work to protect under-water heritage. The court cases that ensue stretch on for years. Are finders keepers, or do the ships belong to the countries that made them and sent them sailing centuries ago? Where once salvors and archaeologists worked side by side, now they belong to opposing, and equally contemptuous, tribes.
F) Nearly three million vessels lie wrecked on the Earth's ocean floor—from old canoes to the Titanic— and likely less than one percent have been explored. Some—like an ancient Roman ship found off Antikythera, Greece, dated between 70 and 60 BC and carrying astonishingly sophisticated gears and dials for navigating by the sun—are critical to a new understanding of our past. No wonder there is an eternal stirring among everybody from salvors to scholars to find them.
G) In May 2016, a salvor named Bobby Pritchett, president of Global Marine Exploration (GME) in Tampa, Florida, announced that he had discovered scattered remains of a ship buried a kilometer off Cape Canaveral. Over the prior three years, he and his crew had obtained 14 state permits to survey a nearly 260-square-kilometer area off the cape; they worked 250 days a year, backed by investor funds of, he claims, US $4 million. It was hard work. Crew members were up at dawn, dragging sensors from their expedition vessels back and forth, day in and day out, year after year, to detect metal of any kind. Using computer technology, Pritchett and his crew created intricate, color-coded maps marked with the GPS coordinates of thousands of finds, all invisible under a meter of sand.
H) One day in 2015, the magnetometer(磁力计) picked up metal that turned out to be an iron cannon; when the divers blew the sand away, they also discovered a more precious bronze cannon with markings indicating French royalty and, not far off, a famous marble column carved with the coat of arms of France, known from historical paintings. The discovery was cause for celebration. The artifacts indicated the divers had likely found the wreck of La Trinité, a 16th-century French vessel that had been at the center of a bloody battle between France and Spain that changed the fate of the United States of America.
I) And then the legal storm began, with GME and Pritchett pitted against Florida and France. The Sunken Military Craft Act of 2004, a US federal act, protects any vessel that was on a military mission, allowing the originating country to claim their ship even centuries later. In 2018, two long years after Pritchett's discovery, the federal district court ruled in favor of France. For Pritchett, the decision was devastating. Millions of dollars of investor funding and years of labor were lost.
J) But this is far from the first time a salvor has lost all rights to a discovery. In 2012, for instance, Spain won a five-year legal battle against Odyssey Marine Exploration, which had hauled 594,000 gold and silver coins from a Spanish wreck off the coast of Portugal across the Atlantic to the United States. "Treasure hunters can be naive," says attorney David Concannon, who has had several maritime archaeologists as clients and represented two sides in the battles over the Titanic for 20 years. "Many treasure hunters don't understand they are going to have to fight for their rights against a government that has an endless supply of money for legal battles that treasure hunters are likely to lose."
K) Putting an inflated price on artifacts rather than viewing them as cultural and historical treasures that transcend any price is what irritates many archaeologists. For the archaeologist, everything in a wreck matters—hair, fabric, a fragment of a newspaper, rat bones-all things speak volumes. Archaeologists don't want artifacts ending up in a private collection instead of taking humanity on a journey of understanding.
L) George Bass is one of the pioneers of under-water archaeology, and a researcher at Texas A&M University. He has testified in court against treasure hunters, but says archaeology is not without its own serious problems. He believes archaeologists need to do a better job themselves instead of routinely criticizing treasure hunters. "Archaeology has a terrible reputation for not publishing enough on its excavations(发掘) and finds," he says. Gathering data, unearthing and meticulously preserving and examining finds, verifying identity and origin, piecing together the larger story, and writing and publishing a comprehensive paper or book can take decades. A bit cynically, Bass describes colleagues who never published because they waited so long they became ill or died. Who is more at fault, Bass asks, the professional archaeologist who carefully excavates a site and never publishes on it or the treasure hunter who locates a submerged wreck, salvages part, conserves part, and publishes a book on the operation?
M) Pritchett concedes that his find deserves careful excavation and preservation. "I think what I found should go in a museum," he says. "But I also think I should get paid for what I found." Indeed, it's a bit of a mystery why governments, archaeologists, and treasure hunters can't work together—and why salvors aren't at least given a substantial finder's fee before the original owner takes possession of the vessel and its artifacts.

P1 Could you get by without using the internet for four and a half years? That's exactly what singer and actress Selena Gomez has done in a bid to improve her mental health.

P2 She has spoken extensively about the relationship between her social media usage and her mental wellbeing, recalling feeling like "an addict" when she became Instagram's most followed user in 2016. "Taking a break from social media was the best decision that I've ever made for my mental health", says she. "The unnecessary hate and comparisons went away once I put my phone down."

P3 Ditching the web at large, however, is a far more subtle and complicated prospect. The increasing digitisation of our society means that everything from paying a gas bill to plotting a route to a friend's house and even making a phone call is at the mercy of your internet connection. Actively opting out of using the internet becomes a matter of privilege. Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.

P4 Ms Gomez's multi-millionaire status has allowed her to take the "social" out of social media, so she can continue to leverage her enormous fame while keeping the trolls(恶意挑衅的帖子) at bay. The fact that she's still the second most-followed woman on Instagram suggests it's entirely possible to maintain a significant web profile to promote various projects—by way of a dedicated team—without being exposed to the cruel comments, hate mail and rape or death threats.

P5 It goes without saying that this is fundamentally different from how the rest of us without beauty deals and films to publicise use the likes of Instagram, TikTok and Twitter, but even the concept of a digital detox(戒瘾) requires having a device and connectivity to choose to disconnect from.

P6 The UK's digital divide has worsened over the past two years, leaving poorer families without broadband connections in their homes. Digital exclusion is a major threat to wider societal equality in the UK, so witnessing companies like Facebook championing the metaverse(元宇宙) as the next great frontier when school children are struggling to complete their homework feels particularly irritating.

P7 Consequently, it's worth bearing in mind that while deleting all social media accounts will undoubtedly make some feel infinitely better, many other people benefit from the strong sense of community that sharing platforms can breed.

P8 Internet access will continue to grow in importance as we edge further towards web 3.0, and greater resources and initiatives are needed to provide the underprivileged with the connectivity they desperately need to learn, work and live. It's crucial that people who feel that social media is having a detrimental effect on their mental health are allowed to switch off and for those living in digital exclusion to be able to switch on in the first place.

P1 Psychologists have long been in disagreement as to whether competition is a learned or a genetic component of human behavior. Whatever it is, you cannot but recognize the effect competition is exerting in academics and many other areas of contemporary life.

P2 Psychologically speaking, competition has been seen as an inevitable consequence of human drives. According to Sigmund Freud, humans are born screaming for attention and full of organic drives for fulfillment in various areas. Initially, we compete for the attention of our parents. Thereafter, we are at the mercy of a battle between our base impulses for self-fulfillment and social and cultural norms which prohibit pure indulgence.

P3 Current work in anthropology(人类学) has suggested, however, that this view of the role of competition in human behavior may be incorrect. Thomas Hobbes, one of the great philosophers of the seventeenth century, is perhaps best remembered for his characterization of the "natural world," that is, the world before the imposition of the will of humanity, as being "nasty, brutish, and short." This image of the pre-rational world is still widely held, reinforced by Charles Darwin's highly influential work, The Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage. Origin of Species, which established the doctrine of natural selection. This doctrine, which takes for granted that those species best able to adapt to and master the natural environment in which they live will survive, has suggested that the struggle for survival is an inherent human trait which determines a person's success. Darwin's theory has even been summarized as "survival of the fittest"—a phrase Darwin himself never used—further highlighting competition's role in success. As it has often been pointed out, however, there is nothing in the concept of natural selection that suggests that competition is the most successful strategy for "survival of the fittest." Darwin asserted in The Origin of Species that the struggles he was describing should be viewed as metaphors and could easily include dependence and cooperation.

P4 Many studies have been conducted to test the importance placed on competition as opposed to other values, such as cooperation—by various cultures, and generally conclude that Americans uniquely praise competition as natural, inevitable, and desirable. In 1937, the world-renowned anthropologist Margaret Mead published Cooperation and Competition among Primitive Peoples, based on her studies of several societies that did not prize competition, and, in fact, seemed at times to place a negative value on it. One such society was the Zuni Indians of Arizona, and they, Mead found, valued cooperation far more than competition. After studying dozens of such cultures, Mead's final conclusion was that competitiveness is a culturally created aspect of human behavior, and that its prevalence in a particular society is relative to how that society values it. 51. What does the author think is easy to see in many areas of contemporary life? A) The disagreement on the inevitability of competition. B) The consequence of psychological investigation. C) The effect of human drives. D) The impact of competition.

writing.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence “Nowadays parents are increasingly aware that allowing kids more freedom to explore and learn on their own helps foster their independence and boost their confidence.” You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay.You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words(not including the sentence given).
writing.model: Nowadays parents are increasingly aware that allowing kids more freedom to explore and learn on their own helps foster their independence and boost their confidence. This shift in parenting reflects a valuable truth: children grow strongest not when every step is arranged for them, but when they are trusted to try, fail, and try again. To begin with, freedom teaches independence in a way no lecture ever could. A child who is allowed to plan a weekend trip, cook a simple meal, or solve a quarrel with friends gradually learns to rely on his own judgment. Take my younger cousin, for example. When his mother stopped correcting his every homework mistake and let him check the answers himself, his grades slowly improved, and, more importantly, he began tackling new problems without fear. Each small success became a brick building his confidence. In this way, granting children the room to explore freely is not a risk but a wise investment. As a result, they mature into adults who dare to think, decide, and stand on their own feet.

translation.source: 随着经济与社会的发展，中国人口结构发生了显著变化，逐渐步入老龄化社会。中国老年人口将持续增加，人口老龄化趋势将更加明显。为了应对人口老龄化带来的种种挑战，国家正积极采取措施，加大对养老的支持。通过改革社会保障(social security)制度，政府不断增加社会保障经费，逐步扩大社会保障覆盖范围，使更多老年人受益。政府还鼓励各种社会团体为老年人提供服务。在政府和社会团体的共同努力下，老年人将生活得更加幸福。
translation.reference: With the development of the economy and society, China’s population structure has undergone remarkable changes and is gradually entering an aging society. China’s elderly population will continue to increase, and the trend of population aging will become more pronounced. To cope with the various challenges brought by population aging, the country is actively taking measures to increase its support for elderly care. By reforming the social security system, the government keeps increasing social security funding and gradually expanding its coverage, so that more elderly people can benefit. In addition, the government encourages various social organizations to provide services for the elderly. With the joint efforts of the government and social organizations, the elderly will live a happier life.

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 人口结构作主语 + 发生变化作谓语（主语策略：原句主语） 中文有明确主语 中国人口结构，核心动词是 发生了显著变化，定英文主干为 China’s population structure has undergone remarkable changes。「随着经济与社会的发展」是伴随状语，不进 主干。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 随着…降级为 with 介词短语 + 步入老龄化降级为并列谓语 随着经济与社会的发展 降级成介词短语 With the economic and social development 放句首作 状语；逐渐步入老龄化社会 与前面「发生变化」是同一主语的连续动作，降级成并列谓语 and is gradually entering an aging society，用 and 连接、不另起一句。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 「发生了变化」是到现在为止已出现、且影响延续至今的变化，用现在完成时 has undergone， 比一般过去时更贴；「逐渐步入」是正在进行的趋势，用现在进行时 is entering，与全篇现在时基 调一致。 单复数 「显著变化」不止一处，用复数 changes；society 在 an aging society 中特指一种社会形态，用 单数加冠词 an。 用词 「显著」用 remarkable / significant；「逐渐」用 gradually，对应 逐渐步入，别漏译这个程度 副词。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: With the development of the economy and society, China’s population structure has undergone remarkable changes and is gradually entering an aging society. 2. 中国老年人口将持续增加，人口老龄化趋势将更加明显。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 两个分句各有主语、各立一套主谓（主语策略：原句主语） 这是两个并列分句，各有明确主语：中国老年人口（China’s elderly population）配谓语 will continue to increase；人口老龄化趋势（the trend of population aging）配谓语 will become more pronounced。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 本句结构简单、两并列分句直接 and 连接 无需复杂降级，两个「主语 + will + 动词」的分句用 and 平接即可：…will continue to increase, and the trend of population aging will become more pronounced。这是少数适合用 and 直 接并列的场合，因为两边确是结构对称的独立陈述。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 两个「将」字 将持续增加、将更加明显 都是对未来的预测，偏离全篇现在时基调，改用一般将来 时 will continue / will become。这正是基调允许的『确有需要处偏离』。 单复数与主谓一致 population 作整体概念用单数，谓语 will continue 不受影响（will 无人称变化，但还原 increases 时须配单数）；the trend 单数特指这一趋势，加定冠词 the。 用词 「更加明显」译 more pronounced / more obvious / more evident，比直译 more clear 地 道；「持续增加」用 continue to increase / keep growing。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: China’s elderly population will continue to increase, and the trend of population aging will become more pronounced. 3. 为了应对人口老龄化带来的种种挑战，国家正积极采取措施，加大对养老的支持。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 国家作主语 + 采取措施作谓语（主语策略：原句主语） 主语是 国家（the country / the government），核心动作是 正积极采取措施，定主干 the country is actively taking measures。「为了应对…挑战」是目的状语，「加大对养老的支持」 是采取措施的具体内容/目的，均不进主干。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 为了应对…降级为 to 不定式 + 加大支持降级为 to 不定式/并列 为了应对人口老龄化带来的种种挑战 降级成 To cope with the various challenges brought by population aging 作句首目的状语，其中「带来的」用过去分词 brought by 作后置定语修饰 challenges；加大对养老的支持 是采取措施的目的，可降级成 to increase its support for elderly care，与主句构成「采取措施以加大支持」。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 「正积极采取措施」是当下正在进行的动作，用现在进行时 is actively taking，贴合「正」字，也 合全篇现在时基调。 单复数 「种种挑战」强调多种，用复数 challenges，搭配 various；measures 采取多项措施用复数。 介词搭配 「应对挑战」用 cope with / deal with / address；「对养老的支持」用 support for（不是 support to）；「养老」译 elderly care / old-age care。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: To cope with the various challenges brought by population aging, the country is actively taking measures to increase its support for elderly care. 4. 通过改革社会保障(social security)制度，政府不断增加社会保障经费，逐步扩大社会保障覆盖 范围，使更多老年人受益。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 政府作主语 + 增加经费、扩大范围作并列谓语（主语策略：原句主语） 主语是 政府（the government），有两个并列核心动作：不断增加社会保障经费、逐步扩大社会 保障覆盖范围，定主干 the government keeps increasing the social security funding and gradually expanding its coverage。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 通过…降级为 by 短语 + 使…受益降级为 so that 从句/分词 通过改革社会保障\(social security\)制度 是手段，降级成 By reforming the social security system 作方式状语放句首；使更多老年人受益 是前面动作的结果，降级成结果状语，用 so that more elderly people can benefit 或现在分词 benefiting more elderly people 挂在主句后。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 「不断增加」「逐步扩大」是持续进行的现状，用一般现在时 keeps increasing / gradually expands，合全篇基调。 单复数与受益主体 「更多老年人」用复数 more elderly people；「受益」用 benefit（不及物，benefit from 或单 用 benefit），主语是老年人，写成 more elderly people can benefit。 用词与冠词 「社会保障经费」译 social security funding / funds；「覆盖范围」译 coverage，特指该制度的 覆盖面用 its coverage；「逐步」gradually、「不断」continuously / keep doing，对应 不断增 加、逐步扩大 不漏译程度词。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: By reforming the social security system, the government keeps increasing social security funding and gradually expanding its coverage, so that more elderly people can benefit. 5. 政府还鼓励各种社会团体为老年人提供服务。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 政府作主语 + 鼓励作谓语 + 社会团体作宾语（主语策略：原句主语） 主语 政府，核心动词 鼓励，宾语 各种社会团体，定主干 the government also encourages various social organizations。后面「为老年人提供服务」是社会团体要做的事。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 为老年人提供服务降级为 to 不定式作宾补 为老年人提供服务 降级成不定式 to provide services for the elderly，作宾语 social organizations 的补足语，构成 encourage…to do 结构，无需另起分句。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 「鼓励」是政府当前的做法，用一般现在时 encourages，第三人称单数主语 the government 后 动词加 s，合全篇基调。 主谓一致 主语 the government 是第三人称单数，谓语用 encourages（加 s），是主体考生常漏的一致问 题。 介词搭配 「为老年人提供服务」用 provide services for the elderly（provide sth for sb）或 provide the elderly with services（provide sb with sth），两种搭配都对，别混成 provide services to 之外 的乱搭。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The government also encourages various social organizations to provide services for the elderly. 6. 在政府和社会团体的共同努力下，老年人将生活得更加幸福。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 老年人作主语 + 生活得更幸福作谓语（主语策略：原句主语） 主语是 老年人（the elderly），核心是 将生活得更加幸福，定主干 the elderly will live a happier life / the elderly will live more happily。「在…共同努力下」是条件/方式状语，不进 主干。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 在共同努力下降级为 with 介词短语 在政府和社会团体的共同努力下 降级成 With the joint efforts of the government and social organizations 作句首状语；「生活得更加幸福」用 live a happier life（形容词比较级修饰 life） 或 live more happily（副词比较级）表达。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 「将生活得更幸福」是对未来的预期，用一般将来时 will live，偏离现在时基调，与第 2 句的 will 同理。 比较级 「更加幸福」要用比较级：a happier life 或 more happily，别漏掉比较级只写 happy。 专名统一与单复数 social organizations 须与第 4、5 句沿用同一译法、用复数；efforts 用复数；the elderly 作主语 指一类人，视作复数。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: With the joint efforts of the government and social organizations, the elderly will live a happier life. 英语六级 2023年12月·第2套 · 全卷构成 Part III Part III Part III Part III
